To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the WSC data are assimilated into a land surface model using ES algorithm; and the results are in agreement with ground observations and with previous studies.
the assimilation scheme is able to estimate the main vegetation parameters of the model, and to improve the simulated water fluxes.
the assimilation of coarse remote sensing radar data can be used to control the trajectory (i.e., to estimate parameters) of a Sahelian land surface scheme.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a land surface model (LSM) that can assimilate coarse remote sensing observations (e.g., WSC) to estimate the state and fluxes of the land surface.
the development and application of an assimilation method to estimate land surface parameters using coarse WSC data.
the development of a new method for the estimation of land surface parameters in the context of the Sahel.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proposed assimilation scheme can provide an efficient way to estimate land surface parameters in semi-arid ecosystems.
the assimilation of coarse remote sensing data can improve significantly land surface model performances.
the proposed method is a good way to control a simple land surface model and that the assimilation scheme is well suited for this kind of problem.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the use of coarse resolution WSC data can be used to improve the simulation of Sahelian land surface processes.
WSC data assimilated in a simple Sahelian model coupled to a RTM allows a better estimation of water fluxes and herbaceous mass.
the assimilation of ERS wind observations into a Sahelian land surface and RTM is a valuable approach to improve the estimation of the Sahelian land surface state and its water cycle.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the assimilation of coarse remote sensing data is a valuable way to control the behaviour of a simple land surface model and to improve the estimation of land surface fluxes.
the WSC data can be used to control the evolution of the land surface variables.
WSC observations can be used to improve the simulation of Sahelian ecosystems and that the assimilation of such observations can be performed with an efficient stochastic optimization scheme.
